events.title: General Motors Is Founded
events.description: William C. Durant founded General Motors in Flint, Michigan, with Charles Stewart Mott among the company's early figures. Durant began by bringing Buick and other automakers together under one corporate roof.
events.significance: GM grew into one of the world's largest automakers. It shaped the American auto industry and the wider industrial economy of the 20th century.

events.title: Wall Street Bombing
events.description: A horse-drawn wagon packed with explosives blew up in the heart of New York's financial district at midday. The blast killed 38 people and injured hundreds more.
events.significance: It was the deadliest act of its kind on American soil up to that date. No one was ever definitively held responsible, and the case remains unsolved.

events.title: Malaysia Is Formed
events.description: The Federation of Malaya joined with Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore to create the new nation of Malaysia. The merger redrew the political map of Southeast Asia.
events.significance: The date is still celebrated as Malaysia Day. Singapore left the federation two years later and became an independent republic.

events.title: Sabra and Shatila Massacre Begins
events.description: A Lebanese Christian Phalangist militia entered the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps in the Beirut area. Over about three days it killed hundreds to thousands of mostly Palestinian civilians.
events.significance: The massacre drew worldwide condemnation. It became one of the most notorious atrocities of the Lebanese Civil War and changed the debate over responsibility in the conflict.
